paragraphs: First I went to Lund University in Sweden for two months. In the first month I rotated through surgery, mainly seeing cases of pancreatic cancer and esophageal cancer. There were differences from Japan, such as having tea time during surgery, which was interesting. I was also impressed that they centralise hospitals to secure doctor manpower and achieve work-life balance. In fact, even though it was surgery, about half of the doctors were women.

In the second month I rotated through pediatrics. The standard weight of newborns was 3,500 g, and I felt the difference in physique from Japan. The clerkship was mostly just going around outpatient clinics and rounds, but the pediatric cardiology doctor taught me very enthusiastically, and I became quite strong in that field. As an impression of the clerkship in Sweden, in terms of procedures one may be able to learn more in Japan. However, Lund is a town that many international students from various countries come to. In terms of coming into contact with the cultures and ideas of various countries and broadening one's outlook, nothing beats Lund. In fact, I can still do my best in Japan now on the basis of the motivation that rose in Sweden.

After Lund I went to Dalhousie University in Canada. This university is not a partner school, but I desperately searched and applied because I wanted to go to a university in an English-speaking country as well. In Canada too I rotated through surgery. Here there was an atmosphere of trying to have students learn procedures, and I took part in most operations as first assistant and learned many procedures such as suturing. Also, while desperately trying to keep up with native English, I think my English improved considerably. Canada is also a country with abundant nature. Even I, who normally am not much moved by nature, found many tourist spots that moved me, so I hope everyone can share this feeling.

Lastly, when you consider studying abroad, you will probably often hear various disadvantages from those around you. But most of my classmates and seniors who went abroad all say in unison that they were glad they went. I too can say with confidence that it was a very meaningful experience. To those who feel they want to study abroad, I hope you will go without minding the noise around you.
